headline: Spotify lets parents exclude kids' music from recommendations and Wrapped
summary: The streaming giant is rolling out a new feature that allows users to filter out music they don't want associated with their account, finally addressing a common parental request.
details: Spotify has announced a new feature designed to give users more control over their listening experience, particularly for parents. This update allows individuals to exclude specific music, such as children's songs or content they simply dislike, from influencing their recommendations and their annual Spotify Wrapped.

The move comes after years of user requests for such functionality. Many parents found that music their children listened to was skewing their own algorithmic recommendations and impacting their Wrapped data, leading to a less personalized experience.

This new setting will be available within the Spotify app's settings menu. Users can toggle it on to ensure that the music played by family members, especially younger ones, does not affect their own music discovery or year-end summary.

The feature aims to provide a cleaner, more tailored listening journey for every user, acknowledging that listening habits can be influenced by shared devices or household members. It's a significant step towards greater personalization on the platform.
